items.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Leopold Stokowski... took me aside... And he said he’d like to have me with his orchestra down in Houston

ctx.x: Right at that time, when you were about to graduate from Eastman, what were your career aspirations then?

Well I thought that making gigs is one thing, you know twenty bucks a night and you play your brains out and have a great time, but I wasn’t sure that that’s what I wanted to do. And seeing what appeared to be a relatively stable financial environment as classical orchestral playing, I said well I’ll spend four years here and this is my last two weeks at school I might as well find out what the deal is. And Leopold Stokowski, who was one of the guest conductors of the Philharmonic when I was there, took me aside…
And the young black musician nowadays is not going to be encouraged to go that route anyway.
